questions.question: Jake weeds the garden ______
Gabe has blond, ______
Ella fell off her bike. Now she has ______
Olivia can sing and dance. She’s very ______
Eddy is always making things. He has a great ______
Maddie won. She had the highest ______
How are you different from one of your relatives? Are you taller, older, faster?
questions.given: I'm faster in my relatives, but I'm not taller.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I am taller than my cousin Susan.
questions.comment: The comparative needs "than", not "in": marked wrong, with "than" written in above it.
questions.correction: I'm faster than my relatives, but I'm not taller.

questions.question: How often do you do homework?
questions.answer: Sample answer: I do homework every day.
questions.comment: Accepted, with "do" written in — you do homework, you study a subject.

questions.question: What is an example of something that is biodegradable?
questions.given: Wood is biodegradable, you can use lots of time.
questions.answer: Sample answer: A paper bag is biodegradable.
questions.comment: Accepted. A comma splice ("biodegradable, you can"), but the idea is right.

questions.question: She ______ go to the doctor because she is sick.
I think math is ______ difficult than science.
I think hot peppers are ______ than pumpkins.
questions.comment: Left blank. "better" was the one word never crossed off the box.

questions.question: People ______ read by candlelight.
I have an uncle ______ likes ice cream.
Soccer is a sport ______ people play all over the world.
The ______ the race, the more you have to practice.
My sister is ______ than I am. She is 10 years old and I am 8 years old.
What are you doing on Sunday? I’m ______ my grandparents.
What ______ you like for dinner? I’d like a hamburger.
I have a stomachache. What ______ I do?
My mother burned ______ on the stove.
In your opinion, what is the ______ TV show?
In the future, sea animals ______ disappear if the oceans are not clean.
Do you want a glass of orange juice? (would like)
questions.given: what would you like to drink juice ?
questions.answer: Would you like a glass of orange juice?
questions.comment: Accepted. "What" was crossed out and "Would" written in — the question starts with the modal.
questions.correction: Would you like a glass of orange juice?

questions.question: My brother likes to wash the dishes. I like to take out the trash. (but)
questions.given: My brother likes to wash the dishes, but, I like to take out the trash.
questions.answer: My brother likes to wash the dishes, but I like to take out the trash.
questions.comment: Marked wrong for the comma after "but".
questions.correction: My brother likes to wash the dishes, but I like to take out the trash.

questions.answer: People used to play board games.

questions.question: Our bodies work hard to keep us healthy.
You can see germs with your bare eyes.
Some germs can live for two hours on your desk.
It is important to wash your hands with soap to stay healthy.
The twilight zone is ______ the sunlit zone.
questions.comment: Correct — he wrote "a" first and corrected it to "b" himself.

questions.question: Some of the fish in the twilight zone make their own ______.
Fish in the twilight zone are ______ than fish in the sunlit zone.
Scientists used to think that ______ in the twilight zone.
questions.given: a. there was a lot of life
questions.answer: b. there wasn’t a lot of life

options: a. there was a lot of life
b. there wasn’t a lot of life
c. only the biggest fish lived

questions.question: Someday there may be ______ in the twilight zone.
What is the twilight zone like?

questions.answer: Sample answer: The twilight zone is cold and dark.
questions.comment: Full marks. Content is right, with spelling and preposition slips corrected in the margin.

questions.question: What is different about the fish in the twilight zone?
questions.given: Twilight zone fishes are stranger than Sunlit zone, but more animals are living Sunlit Zone.
questions.answer: Sample answer: The fish can make their own light. / The fish look stranger.
questions.comment: Full marks. The comparison is there despite the phrasing.

questions.question: What do you think will happen to the twilight zone in the future?
questions.given: Someday, fishing Compaines may kill so many fish that not enough fish. If they do lots of overfishing, fishes and Sea animals will disoppier in our world.
questions.answer: Sample answer: I think there will be overfishing in the twilight zone.

questions.question: (a)  Soccer — how many million people play?
(b)  Soccer — in how many countries?
(c)  Soccer — how many billion people watch?
(d)  Baseball — how many million people play?
(e)  Baseball — in how many countries?
(f)  Baseball — how many million people watch?
questions.comment: Marked wrong; the number on the track is 20.

questions.question: Which sport has more players?
questions.given: Soccer has more players than baseball because Soccer has two hundred sixty five millions of players are playing.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Soccer has more players than baseball.
questions.comment: Full marks — the comparison with "than" is there.

questions.question: Which sport is played in more countries?
questions.given: Soccer is more countries are playing than baseball. Two hundred of countlies are played.
questions.answer: Sample answer: Soccer is played in more countries than baseball.
questions.comment: Half marks. The comparison is there, but the sentence needs the passive: "played in".
questions.correction: Soccer is played in more countries than baseball. It is played in two hundred countries.
